description: Accept a file for a pitch, validate it, send it to the document store and record the result. Validation runs before the store is called, so a rejected file never leaves the process. The file lands in a folder keyed by the pitch's identifier rather than its title, because a retitled pitch must not orphan its files. The record is written only after the store confirms the upload: a row pointing at a file that was never stored reads as success until someone clicks it, which is worse than the failure it hides.
expectedBehavior: A file within the size limit and of an allowed type is stored and a record is created
The stored file is byte-identical to what was uploaded
An oversized file or a disallowed type is refused with a message naming the limit, and the store is never called
A store failure returns an error and creates no record
Editing rights are required; the check is server-side
The folder is keyed by the pitch's identifier, so renaming the pitch does not move or orphan files
verificationSteps: With the fake store forced to fail, upload a file and confirm the response is an error and the pitch's attachment list is unchanged
Upload an oversized file and a disallowed type, and assert the fake store recorded no call
Against the real tenant, upload a file and compare a checksum of the source with a checksum of the stored file; record both
